chunks: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan, from Bakr ibn Salih, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id who said:

Abu Ja'far the Second (peace be upon him) was asked: 'Is it permissible to say about God that He is a thing?' He said: 'Yes. It removes Him from the two limits — the limit of ta'til (denial of attributes) and the limit of tashbih (anthropomorphism).'

key_terms.التَّشْبِيه: Tashbih — the theological error of anthropomorphism, likening God to created beings
key_terms.التَّعْطِيل: Ta'til — the theological error of stripping God of all attributes, essentially denying His existence or reality
key_terms.الْحَدَّيْن: The two limits/extremes — referring to ta'til and tashbih as the two forbidden theological extremes
key_terms.شَيْء: A thing/entity — used in Islamic theology to affirm God's existence and reality without limiting Him

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in Islam to say God is a 'thing', and what does the Imam say about it?
ai.summary: Imam Muhammad al-Jawad (peace be upon him), the ninth Imam, was asked whether it is theologically permissible to use the word 'thing' (shay') in reference to God. The Imam answered affirmatively, explaining that calling God 'a thing' serves as a middle path: it affirms God's real existence against ta'til (the heretical position of stripping God of all attributes, rendering Him purely abstract or non-existent), while simultaneously refusing the anthropomorphic extreme of tashbih (likening God to created things). This hadith reflects a core principle of Shia kalām (theology): God's attributes must be affirmed, but His uniqueness must also be preserved — He is a 'thing unlike things'.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Husayn Bin Al Hassan, from Bakr Bin Salih, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed who said,

‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> the 2<sup>nd</sup> was asked, ‘Is it allowed for one to say for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> that He<sup>azwj</sup> is a thing?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes. Take Him<sup>azwj</sup> out from the two limitations – the limitation of temporariness and the limit of resemblance’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn ‘Abdallah has narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il from al-Husayn ibn al-Hassan from Bakr ibn Salih from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id who said that I asked Imam abu Ja‘far, the second (a.s.) the following. “Is it permissible to say that Allah is a thing?”
The Imam replied, “Yes, because it removes two kinds of limitations, the limitation of being forgotten altogether and that of considering Him like other things.”
